summary: Washington's oldest lighthouse, lit in 1856 at the mouth of the Columbia; its first-order lens went to North Head in 1898 and a fourth-order light still shines.

access.note: On Coast Guard property; the trail to the lighthouse was closed to the public as of a July 2020 Coast Guard notice.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NRHP says the tower was completed in 1854 and lit in 1856; LighthouseFriends says construction resumed about two years after the 1853 Oriole wreck and the tower was dismantled and rebuilt. The first-lit date, 15 October 1856, agrees across sources.

notes_for_editor: Thin on primary sources: the 1850s-70s Light-House Board reports are not in the corpus, so keeper anecdotes, logbook entries, the 1852 contract and the Oriole wreck rest on LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased, one logbook phrase quoted) and HistoryLink. Disagreements flagged in the text: build timeline (NRHP 1854 vs LF rebuild), lens origin (NRHP/HistoryLink 1822 French lens from New England vs LF Sautter), tower material (USLHS dressed stone vs brick), life-saving station date (LF 1871 vs NRHP 1877), fate of the old bell (LF West Point vs HistoryLink Warrior Rock), whether the 1871 blast shattered the bell or bell house. The 1891-92 volume's printed page number is unconfirmed (scan p.233, printed p.170?). Report year 1896 item 1093 (concrete retaining wall) was found but not used. The 1921 gale: the 126 mph reading in the Bulletin was at North Head, so it is not used. Roster lines taken from USLHS; no position-matched OCR tables. Today status relies on a July 2020 notice and LF; confirm current access. Wikipedia used for leads only. Tower build timeline: no Light-House Board report from the 1850s was available to settle it. Roster lines for Boyd (1854) predate first lighting (1856), as printed. The 1891 report page 170 is read from the OCR page head.
